# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-18 (Extended v137)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Summer Year 5—Louis Philippe's reign)**: Paris—Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Rue de la Verrerie (Courfeyrac's residence); Rue Plumet (Valjean's primary house); Rue de Babylone (secret passage exit); Rue de l'Homme Armé (secondary apartment); Rue de l'Ouest (secondary apartment); Faubourg Saint-Antoine; Faubourg Saint-Marceau; wine-shops (Seven Billiards, Corinthe, Richefeu's, Café Musain); schools; Boulevard de l'Hôpital; Jardin des Plantes; Luxembourg; Saint-Jacques-du-Haut-Pas church; Dunstead (harbor town in English provinces); Staveford. **Environmental details**: Frost silvered hedges; chalked crooked sun on forge wall; rain threatened; wind carries salt/tar scent; road ruts and puddles after thaw; light goes early; smoke lies flat; bells ring for vespers; baker's boy often late; lines at oven grow long; cart loaded with turnips creaks past well; children chase hoop shrieking; dogs bark at nothing; gulls quarrel over fish heads by steps; chimneys smoke flat over fields; bees hum in lavender behind parsonage.

## Primary Locations
**RUE PLUMET HOUSE (Valjean's primary residence, October 1829-present)**: Single-story pavilion in deserted Rue Plumet with garden approximately one-and-a-half acres. Two ground-floor rooms, two first-floor chambers, downstairs kitchen, upstairs boudoir, attic. Behind pavilion: narrow courtyard, low building (two rooms, cellar) for concealing inhabitants. Secret-spring door masked in building communicates via long narrow paved winding corridor (hemmed by lofty walls, hidden between garden enclosures and cultivated land) to Rue de Babylone quarter-league distant with another secret-lock door. Originally built mid-last-century by Paris Parliament chief justice as mistress-house; passed through bankruptcy; remained uninhabited and furnished with old furniture; yellow illegible notice on garden wall since 1819. October 1829: Valjean (as M. Fauchelevent, independent gentleman) hired and repaired house. **Garden characteristics (Summer Year 5)**: Left uncultivated deliberately to avoid attention; left to itself over fifty years, now extraordinary and charming. In winter: thicket black, dripping, bristling; silvery snail tracks visible on cold yellow leaf carpet. All seasons: breathes melancholy, contemplation, solitude, liberty, absence of man, presence of God. Ancient padlocked gate twisted, tottering, fastened to two moss-covered pillars; forty years of dreamers gazed through bars. Former coquettish garden transformed: no arbors, bowling greens, tunnels, grottos remain; magnificent disheveled obscurity falls like veil; Paphos made Eden; element of repentance rendered retreat wholesome; flower-girl now offers blossom to soul; garden returned to virginity and modesty; nature filled with shade, arranged for love. **Door on Rue de Babylone**: Box for letters/papers; receives only tax-collector notices and guard summons. Three inhabitants (Valjean, Cosette, Toussaint) receive neither papers nor letters. **Access strategy**: Neither Valjean, Cosette, nor Toussaint enter/emerge except via Rue de Babylone door.

**VALJEAN'S OTHER APARTMENTS**: Rue de l'Homme Armé (poor appearance); Rue de l'Ouest (poor appearance). Both remote from each other and Rue Plumet. Strategy: rotate residence monthly/six-weeks, served by porters, posing as gentleman from suburbs with temporary resting-place in town.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette: Life at Rue Plumet (October 1829-present)
**Valjean's decision and convent departure**: Recognized necessity of leaving convent after five years; anguish at requiring Cosette's departure, but concluded danger insufficient to condemn her to cloister. Demanded audience with Reverend Prioress; fabricated story of inheritance from deceased brother. Offered five thousand francs to community as indemnity for Cosette's five years free education.

**Daily life and routine**: Cosette taught housekeeping in convent, now regulates household expenditure (modest). **Every day**: Valjean puts arm through Cosette's, takes her for walk—usually Luxembourg (least frequented walk). **Every Sunday**: Takes Cosette to mass at Saint-Jacques-du-Haut-Pas (poor quarter, long way off). Valjean bestows alms largely there; poor people surround him in church. This drew Thénardier's epistle: "To the benevolent gentleman of the church of Saint-Jacques-du-Haut-Pas." Valjean fond of taking Cosette to visit poor and sick. **No stranger ever enters house**. Toussaint brings provisions; Valjean fetches water from nearby fountain on boulevard. Wood and wine stored in half-subterranean hollow lined with rock-work near Rue de Babylone, formerly chief-justice's grotto.

**Valjean's clothing and disguise**: When going out with Cosette: dressed as retired officer. When going out alone (generally at night): workingman's trousers and blouse; cap concealing face. Precaution and humility both. **National Guard service**: M. Fauchelevent, independent gentleman, belongs to national guard (registered in census of 1831). **Three or four times a year** dons uniform, mounts guard willingly—correct disguise mixing him with everyone yet leaving him solitary. Attained sixtieth birthday (age of legal exemption) but does not appear over fifty; no desire to escape service nor quibble with authority; possesses no civil status, concealing name, identity, age, everything. Sum of ambition: resembling any other man who paid taxes. **Ideal**: within, angel; without, bourgeois.

**Valjean and Fantine (deceased mother)**: When Cosette was small, Valjean willing to talk of her mother; when she became young girl, impossible for him to do so. Felt certain religious horror at letting Fantine's shadow enter Cosette's thought; feared placing third in their destiny. Thought Fantine's modesty, having violently quitted her during lifetime, returned after death to watch in indignation over peace of dead woman and keep her in grave. Felt himself overwhelmed with silence regarding Fantine.

## Cosette's Coming of Age (Summer Year 5)
**Physical transformation**: **Beautiful for tolerably long time before aware of it herself.** Skin grown white, hair lustrous, blue eyes gained unaccustomed splendor. Consciousness of beauty burst upon her like sudden daylight. **Three months after mirror incident (Excerpt 1089)**: Gave cry at looking-glass—dazzled herself. Others noticed: Toussaint declared her pretty; passerby remarked "Pretty, but badly dressed." Descended to garden thinking herself queen, hearing birds sing (though winter), seeing sky gilded, sun among trees, flowers in thickets, wild, distracted, inexpressible delight.

**Psychological and social consequences (Excerpt 1090-1093)**: Gaining knowledge of beauty, lost grace of ignoring it. An exquisite grace lost: beauty enhanced by ingenuousness is ineffable; nothing adorable as dazzling innocent creature holding key to paradise without consciousness. What lost in ingenuous grace, gained in pensive serious charm. Whole person permeated with joy of youth, innocence, beauty breathed forth splendid melancholy. **Coquetry awakened**: Conceived horror for merinos and shame for plush hat. Father never refused her anything. Acquired whole science of bonnet, gown, mantle, boot, cuff, stuff in fashion, becoming color—science making Parisian woman charming, deep, dangerous. **First outing in new attire**: Black damask gown and mantle, white crape bonnet; took Valjean's arm, gay, radiant, rosy, proud, dazzling. Asked father how he liked her; Valjean replied "Charming!" in voice resembling bitter envious man.

**Valjean's anguish (Excerpt 1090)**: **Man who passed through all distresses, still bleeding from fate's bruises, almost wicked become almost saint, dragging invisible heavy chain of indefinite misery, whom law had not released and could seize at any moment bringing him from obscurity of virtue to broad daylight of public opprobrium—accepted all, excused all, pardoned all, merely asked of Providence, man, law, society, nature, world: one thing, that Cosette might love him!** Felt change in happy life, life so happy he did not dare move for fear of disarranging something. Beloved by Cosette, he felt healed, rested, appeased, loaded with benefits, recompensed, crowned. Asked nothing more. Had anyone asked "Do you want anything better?" would answer "No." If God asked "Do you desire heaven?" would reply "I should lose by it."

**Relationship with Valjean**: Adored goodman; always at his heels. Where Jean Valjean was, there happiness was. Lived neither in pavilion nor garden; took greater pleasure in paved back courtyard than flower-filled enclosure, in his little lodge with straw-seated chairs than great drawing-room hung with tapestry. Leaned on his arm when went out, proud and happy, in plenitude of heart.

## Cosette and Marius: First Encounter and Evolving Dynamic (Excerpt 1094-1103)
**Two souls prepared (Excerpt 1094)**: **Cosette in her shadow, like Marius in his, all ready to take fire. Destiny, with mysterious and fatal patience, slowly drew together two beings all charged and languishing with stormy electricity of passion, two souls laden with love as clouds laden with lightning, bound to overflow and mingle in look like clouds in flash of fire.** Glance fallen into disrepute in love romances; people hardly dare say two beings fell in love because looked at each other. That is way people do fall in love, only way. Rest is nothing; rest comes afterwards. Nothing more real than great shocks two souls convey by exchange of spark.

**Initial meeting and Cosette's reaction (Excerpt 1095)**: **When their eyes met at last** and said first obscure ineffable things glance lisps, Cosette did not immediately understand. Returned thoughtfully to house in Rue de l'Ouest, where Valjean according to custom came to spend six weeks. **Next morning waking**: Thought of strange young man, so long indifferent and icy, now seemed pay attention to her. Did not appear attention least bit agreeable to her. Somewhat incensed at handsome disdainful individual. Substratum of war stirred within her. Struck her with wholly childish joy: she would take revenge at last. **Psychological assessment of Marius**: Could not refrain saying to herself he had beautiful hair, beautiful eyes, handsome teeth, charming tone of voice conversing with comrades, held himself badly walking but with grace all his own, did not appear stupid, whole person noble, gentle, simple, proud; though seemed poor, his air was fine.

**Cosette's passionate ignorance (Excerpt 1097-1099)**: First thing felt was confused and profound melancholy; soul seemed blackened. Did not know what love was; never heard word uttered in terrestrial sense. At convent, _amour_ (love) replaced by _tambour_ (drum) in profane music books. **Loved with all passion because loved ignorantly.** Did not know whether good/bad, useful/dangerous, eternal/temporary, allowable/prohibited; loved. Would have been astonished by reproach for not sleeping, not eating, heart palpitations, blushing/paling when certain being clad in black appeared in green walk. Replied: "What fault is there of mine in matter in which I have no power and of which I know nothing?" Love suited state of her soul: sort of admiration at distance, mute contemplation, deification of stranger—apparition of youth to youth, dream of nights become reality yet remaining dream, longed-for phantom realized but having neither name, fault, spot, exigence, nor defect. **Distant lover lingering in ideal, chimæra with form.** Any nearer meeting would have alarmed her at first stage, still half immersed in convent's exaggerated mists. Had all fears of children and nuns combined; convent spirit still in process of slow evaporation, made everything tremble. **He was not lover, not even admirer—vision.** Set herself to adoring Marius as something charming, luminous, impossible.

**Cosette's bold initiative (Excerpt 1096)**: Remained on bench; did not approach. This vexed Cosette. One day said to Valjean: "Father, let us stroll about a little in that direction." Seeing Marius did not come to her, she went to him. In such cases, all women resemble Mahomet. First symptom of true love in young man is timidity; in young girl is boldness. Two sexes tending to approach each other, assuming each the other's qualities.

**Marius's awkward conduct and Valjean's suspicions (Excerpt 1100-1103)**: Old Mother Nature warned Valjean in dim way of Marius's presence. Valjean shuddered to bottom of soul; saw nothing, knew nothing, yet scanned with obstinate attention darkness in which he walked, feeling on one side something in process of construction, on other something crumbling away. Marius also warned by same Mother Nature, did all he could keep out of sight of "the father." Yet Valjean sometimes espied him. **Marius's manners no longer natural**: exhibited ambiguous prudence and awkward daring; no longer came quite close as formerly; seated himself at distance and pretended to be reading. **Why did he pretend?** Formerly came in old coat, now wore new one every day; Valjean not sure he did not have hair curled; eyes very queer, wore gloves. **Valjean cordially detested this young man.**

**Valjean's undeclared war (Excerpt 1102-1103)**: Instituted undeclared war against Marius, which Marius with sublime stupidity of passion and age did not divine. Valjean laid host of ambushes: changed hour, changed bench, forgot handkerchief, came alone to Luxembourg. Marius dashed headlong into all snares; to all interrogation marks planted by Valjean, ingenuously answered "yes." But Cosette remained immured in apparent unconcern and imperturbable tranquility, so Valjean concluded: **"That ninny is madly in love with Cosette, but Cosette does not even know that he exists."** Did not discontinue Luxembourg trips (wished nothing out of way, feared arousing Cosette), but during sweet hours while Cosette sent smile to intoxicated Marius perceiving nothing else, Valjean fixed flashing terrible eyes on him. He who finally believed himself incapable of malevolent feeling experienced moments when Marius present where thought becoming savage and ferocious, felt old depths of soul formerly containing wrath opening once more and rising against young man. Unknown craters seemed forming in his bosom.

## Marius Pontmercy: Psychological and Financial Crisis
**Identity and background**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old; three years estranged from grandfather. Paternal legacy: Colonel's instruction regarding Waterloo sergeant Thénardier (Magnon recognized in painting).

**The Ambush Crisis (resolved, April Year 4)**: Jondrette/Thénardier plotted extortion. M. Leblanc escaped: unscrewed coin piece (used as saw), cut cords, brandished red-hot chisel. **"While red-hot iron sank into smoking wound, impassive and almost august, he fixed on Thénardier his beautiful glance, in which there was no hatred, and where suffering vanished in serene majesty."** Dashed from window. Javert positioned outside; took action before Marius's signal. Thénardier woman hurled paving-stone at Javert; Javert ducked; stone struck wall. Javert bore prisoners in three hackney-coaches.

**Aftermath (April Year 4)**: Relocated to Courfeyrac at Rue de la Verrerie; paid quarterly rent, vacated hovel. Two reasons: (1) horror of wicked poor development; (2) avoid lawsuit testimony against Thénardier. Recognized M. Leblanc as Monsieur Fabre (Cosette's biological father). Cosette believed Valjean her father; became convent scholar.

**Financial crisis (Spring-Summer Year 5)**: **First time in life, borrowed five francs from Courfeyrac; now borrows hundred-sou piece (five francs).** Poverty returned; felt icy breath. Old coat becoming impossible; new coat growing old; shirts, hat, boots wearing out.

**Work situation**: Task: turning celebrated German quarrel (Gans and Savigny controversy) into French. Cannot focus: reads four lines, attempts to write one, sees star between himself and paper, abandons task.

**Psychological state**: Passion precipitated him into chimæras without object or bottom. Lost faculty of working toward fixed goal but endowed with more clear-sightedness and rectitude than ever. Judgment almost wholly disassociated from hope. Meditation turns to reproach; reflects dolefully on idleness, paralysis of soul gaining on him, night growing more dense. **No longer even sees sun.** Yet sensations reach him: laundresses beating linen, birds chattering in elm-trees. Happy, even in anguish, is he whom God gave soul worthy of love and unhappiness.

**Marius and Cosette**: She—whole thought. **Periodical five francs a double riddle**: to Courfeyrac who lent, to unknown recipient who received. **Change in demeanor**: Once long indifferent and icy toward Cosette, now pays attention; wears new coat daily, uncertain whether has hair curled, wears gloves, exhibits awkward unnatural behavior—all observed and detested by Valjean.

## M. Mabeuf: Decline and Hope
**Status (Summer Year 5)**: Nearly eighty years old. Health declining; old servant Mother Plutarque ill in bed (unpaid wages fifteen months). Subsists minimally: breakfast two eggs, leaves one for servant; often only meal. No longer smiles; grown morose; no longer receives visitors. Passes Marius sometimes on Boulevard de l'Hôpital; exchange only melancholy sign of head.

**Projects**: _Flora of Cauteretz_ no longer sells. Indigo experiments unsuccessful in Austerlitz garden (bad exposure). Pawned _Flora_ copperplates for Jardin des Plantes corner (good exposure) for indigo trials at own expense. **Three forms of happiness**: Books, garden, indigo. **Plans**: "When I make blueing balls, I'll be rich, withdraw copperplates from pawn-shop, put _Flora_ in vogue with money and newspaper advertisements, buy copy of Pierre de Médine's _Art de Navigier_, edition 1655."

**Mysterious visitor (early Spring Year 5)**: Emerged "tall, slender girl, who drew herself up and stared boldly. Less air of human being than form blossoming from twilight." Unhooked well-chain, withdrew bucket, filled watering-pot, ran barefooted in tattered petticoat among flower-beds distributing water. **"Sound of watering-pot on leaves filled Father Mabeuf's soul with ecstasy."** As he fell asleep: "it came back to him." **Later identified as Éponine**.

## Revolutionary Fermentation (Summer Year 5)
**Enjolras as nexus**: Believed moment at hand: people taking possession of right; revolution majestically taking France. Furnace being heated. Powder train scattered across Paris.

**Network**: Combeferre (eloquence), Feuilly (enthusiasm), Courfeyrac (dash), Bahorel (smile), Jean Prouvaire (melancholy), Joly (science), Bossuet (sarcasms). Created electric spark taking fire nearly everywhere.

**Secret societies and evidence (April Year 4)**: Public cartridge-making. Arrested Pardon. Documents found: printed dialogues, song "Workmen, band together," cartridges, bullet-mould, punch, powder, lead traces. Cipher document: Q, C, D, E = quinturions, centurions, decurions, éclaireurs; date April 15, Year 4.

**Network**: Associations of Friends of People, Society of Rights of Man, Society of Action, Gallic Society, committees, societies for liberty of press, individual liberty, instruction, equal workingmen (levellers, communists), Army of Bastilles. Military: counted on fifty-second, fifth, eighth, thirty-seventh, twentieth light cavalry. Burgundy, southern towns: liberty trees planted. Network spreading like membranes.

## Javert's Outstanding Question and Prison Intelligence Operations
**After M. Leblanc's escape (April Year 4)**: M. Leblanc's identity and whereabouts mystery. **"Assassinated man who flees more suspicious than assassin."**

**Captured**: Babet, Gueulemer. Released: Éponine, Azelma (Les Madelonettes). Montparnasse preferred Éponine over gang work. Three prowlers captured late Year 4.

**Brujon operations (Late Year 4 through February Year 5)**: Released in Charlemagne courtyard. Feigned fever, inquired about ward. End February: executed three commissions (fifty sous total)—homes of three prowlers. Placed solitary month after discovery. **Prison communication**: "Postilion"—moulded bread pallet sent rooftop courtyard-to-courtyard with notes. Babet passed note La Force to Salpêtrière. Woman transmitted to Magnon (bridging Salpêtrière and Les Madelonettes via Éponine).

**Éponine's reconnaissance (Year 5)**: Released Les Madelonettes. Magnon handed Brujon's note. Went to Rue Plumet, recognized gate and garden, observed house, spied, lurked. Brought biscuit (prison symbol) to Magnon, transmitted to Babet's mistress.

## Louis Philippe and Historical Context
**Summer Year 5**: Handsome in old age, graceful. Lacked majesty; no crown, no white hair. Mixture suited 1830. Incorruptible; carried umbrella. Policy domestic; excessive timidity displeasing. Press, tribune, conscience, speech free. **One of best princes ever on throne.** Cloud gathering—strange shade from wraths and systems. Everything hastily stifled, fermenting. Electric tension: first comer brings light. Petty revolts suppressed but bursting afresh—sign vast underlying conflagration.
